name: United Front
role: Opposition Electoral Alliance in East Bengal
contribution: The United Front brought together Awami Muslim League, Krishak Sramik Party, Nizam-e-Islam, and Ganatantri Dal forces around a 21-point programme and defeated the Muslim League in the 1954 East Bengal election.
context: Language-movement aftermath, provincial autonomy demands, and the 1954 East Bengal Legislative Assembly election.
impact: Its landslide victory made East Bengal's provincial electorate a decisive force against centralized Muslim League rule and strengthened the autonomy politics that later fed Bangladesh's national movement.
highlight: The alliance that turned language-era discontent into a major electoral defeat for the Muslim League in East Bengal.
seoTitle: United Front - 1954 East Bengal Election Profile
seoDescription: Profile of the United Front alliance and its role in the 1954 East Bengal election, provincial autonomy, and post-language-movement politics.
shortAnswer: The United Front was the opposition alliance that won the 1954 East Bengal election and challenged Muslim League dominance.

faq.question: Why was the United Front important in 1954?
faq.answer: The United Front converted language-movement and autonomy grievances into a broad electoral challenge, defeating the Muslim League in East Bengal's 1954 provincial election.
